# Implemented capabilities and Praxis proposals

> **Praxis naming:** This page documents **Praxis**, the AIWS workflow engine. Existing `engine/*` source paths, `/engine/...` routes, `aiws-engine/*` protocol identifiers, and existing script names remain unchanged for compatibility.

**Milestone status:** M6 is complete for the D-M6-01 supervised Windows 11 x64 / Node 24 / local SQLite developer profile. M8 is now active (not in this pack): its plan is complete and slice 2 has measured component capacity on two fixed Ubuntu 24.04 Hyper-V guests (Q01, 2026-10-06); every other qualification item and all expanded release/support claims remain open.

This matrix is the first reference for an agent generating application code. **Implemented** means present in the finite-v1 baseline. **M2 source** means implemented in the opt-in handoff-v1 source profile; it ships in the SDK 0.4.0 packages and is absent from the earlier 0.3.0 binaries. **Application-owned** means that the host must supply it. **Proposed** means that no corresponding SDK command or service exists yet; it does not mean the owner-approved design decision is unresolved.

| Capability | Status | Integration rule |
|---|---|---|
| Strict JSON, shared record schemas and decimal accounting | Implemented | Validate at ingress; see wire reference |
| Finite grants, approval fingerprints and dispatch gates | Implemented | Host must authenticate identity and bind policy |
| Deterministic reducer and success assessment | Implemented | No external effects occur during reduction |
| SQLite journal, revision comparison and audit playback | Implemented | One mission per database; replay cost grows with history |
| Coordinator dispatch, UNKNOWN settlement and safe retry | Implemented | Adapter must report truthful external outcomes |
| Recovery segment/epoch and unresolved-attempt report | Implemented | Not a complete worker or target fencing protocol |
| Every trigger kind and fixed-interval catch-up | Implemented | Host supplies event ingress and tick scheduling |
| Every node kind and readiness/completion checks | Implemented | Host supplies task execution and data mapping |
| Input/output JSON Schema checks | Implemented | Restricted schema support; validate artifact bytes separately |
| Control-event traces, metric snapshots and alerts | Implemented | Activity spans and notification routing are host-owned |
| Durable OTLP/HTTP outbox | Implemented | Host must flush it, monitor capacity and manage retention |
| Authentication, human identity and approval inbox | Application-owned | Do not trust an actor string in a command |
| Real test execution and acceptance evidence | Application-owned | SDK checks records, not the truth of an external test report |
| External idempotency, cancellation and read-back | Application-owned | Do not promise exactly-once effects |
| Cron/calendar/DST scheduling and live background workers | Application-owned | Current schedule is UTC fixed interval |
| Nested work-order limits and a protected handoff reserve | M3 source | Separate shared LimitStore; all external dispatch must pass ledger and existing host gates |
| Resumable holds at loop/resource exhaustion | M2/M3 source | Handoff holds plus nested admission gates; finite-v1 LOOP remains terminal FAILED |
| Atomic handoff manifests, delivery claims and acknowledgements | M2 source | Opt-in HandoffStore and authenticated host coordinator |
| Content-addressed artifacts and retention checks | M2 source | Native FileArtifacts; host owns backups, retention and cleanup |
| Automatic restart policy and task-aware pause orchestration | Proposed | Current records do not start/restart processes |
| Governed revisions, task insertion and agent replacement for coding runs | M7 complete (scoped local profile) | Before dispatch or at settled boundaries; versioned and authority-gated; uncertain work held; attached graphs stay immutable |
| Executable revisions of general workflow definitions | Proposed | Revisions exist only as UNBOUND registry records; executable graph edits are disabled |
| Long-history compaction and inspection | Implemented in local engine source | Lossless segments, indexed pages and resumable verification; see [replay limits](./engine-replay-limits.md). Native SDK parser limits remain unchanged |
| Months-long Praxis qualification | Pending | Requires retention, platform and measured capacity evidence |
| Protocol binding abstraction for MCP, A2A and AG-UI | M9.1 complete | Common manifest/catalog/observation boundary is verified; protocol compatibility still requires protocol-specific conformance |
| MCP 2026-07-28 outbound integration | M9.2 complete for synchronous profile | Official v2.2.0 client/server conformance passed for tools/resources/prompts, host auth, timeout/cancel UNKNOWN handling and material capability pinning; Tasks/restartable remote handles are M9.3 |
| MCP Tasks durability/recovery | M9.3 complete | Durable remote-task mapping, persisted restart handoff, polling, revision-bound approved input, cancellation, retry fencing and UNKNOWN reconciliation are verified against pinned official `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-tasks` conformance |
| A2A 1.0 outbound client | M9.4 complete | Durable task identity, fresh Agent Card/skill material pinning, endpoint/time fencing, polling/resubscription and pinned official `@a2a-js/sdk@1.3.0` HTTP+JSON conformance are verified |
| A2A 1.0 Praxis server / Agent Card | M9.5 complete | Authenticated/authorized admission, durable inbound remote↔local identity, official AgentExecutor bridge, status/artifact streaming and terminal-task immutability are verified; A2A events never grant Praxis authority |
| AG-UI 1.0 event projection | M9.6 complete | Projection-only run/step/message/tool/state/activity/subagent events validate against pinned official `@ag-ui/core@1.0.0`; no Praxis mutation or approval/control ingress is introduced |
| AG-UI authenticated human control | M9.7 complete | Standard interrupt/resume maps to the existing authenticated, material-bound, durable Praxis control API; exact retry/receipt recovery and official AG-UI 1.0 schemas are verified |
| Durable cross-protocol registry and observability | M9.8 complete | Immutable binding revisions, separate local/remote identity, evidence correlation, stale-result fencing and allowlisted hashed-identity telemetry are verified |
| Cross-protocol compatibility campaign | M9.9 complete | MCP 2026-07-28 + Tasks, A2A 1.0 and AG-UI 1.0 passed together across 4 profiles, 16 required scenarios and 16 executable checks |
| Cross-language protocol correlation helper | M9.10 complete | TypeScript/Rust/Python source records correlate AIWS/Praxis identity with exact binding revision/remote identity and require `authoritative: false`; not present in older 0.3.0 binary archives |
| Recovery on another machine | Outside agreed Praxis scope | Do not infer distributed failover support |
| Workflow templates, the catalog and the `praxis` run commands | S6 claim A — built, source only | A source-only engine profile, against a host with simulated identity. A host reviews the named workflow templates in its template directory at startup and publishes a workflow catalog; `praxis workflows`, `run`, `runs`, `follow`, `status`, `hold` and `open` read it and create runs over the authenticated loopback control API, and `praxis trust` trusts the host's generated certificate. The catalog, run list and run creation messages are host read models and profile messages at stability `PROVISIONAL`, not wire 1.1.0 records. `praxis` has no decision verbs: a CLI session is refused every decision with `HUMAN_REQUIRED`, and decisions stay in the web view. Until claim B, the only host `praxis` reaches is the simulated one, `example:engine:praxis`, which is not a human gate and never runs real work. See [Praxis CLI](./engine-praxis-cli.md) |
| Passkey owner enrollment, sign-in and CLI sessions | S6 claim B — built, source only | A source-only engine profile: the passkey adapter, WebAuthn hardware-attested owner enrollment against the FIDO MDS3 allowlist, praxis setup, praxis login, praxis logout, praxis serve [--new-certificate], CLI session issuance, 5-minute token rotation with reuse revocation, 30m idle / 8h absolute browser sessions with 5-minute decision window, Authenticators and CLI sessions panels, and certificate rollover pin following. No qualifying hardware authenticator has been checked live (source-only); automated qualification uses Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) virtual authenticators (pm run qualify:engine:passkeys). See [Praxis CLI](./engine-praxis-cli.md) and [S6 milestone record](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/docs/S6-PRAXIS-CLI.md) |
| Governed model binding: agent catalog, model register, credentials and consumption | In progress — M10 contract specified; slices 2, 3, 4, 5 and 7 complete, slice 6's agent setup, login reconnection, reported credential source, exclusive login directory hold and login directory retirement built, source only apart from readiness 2.0.0 | Apart from readiness 2.0.0 (next row), a source-only engine profile; the SDKs carry no other part of it. The built parts are the rows below; of login custody agent setup, the login directory, reconnection, the reported credential source, the exclusive hold and retirement are built, and the rest of it (the restore hold) is not; of the rest of the register, withdrawal and retirement dates are built (their own row below), and corrections and proposals are not. Only the Claude Code host inspector verifies model confinement, and a Claude Code agent, with a delivered key or a subscription login, dispatches only through the Claude Code dispatch adapter. Slice 4's claim, that a human can bind the named Claude Code version with a delivered key to a coding run, that confinement is verified before dispatch and that consumption settles in the ledger, rests on one live run of Claude Code 2.1.287 on Windows ([evidence](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/docs/evidence/m10/slice-4/live-run-20261018/README.md)). Slice 5's claim, that the stop threshold is enforced by the host meter for streamed usage, is for the same agent and demonstrated on recorded runs only, with no model request ([gate review](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/docs/evidence/m10/slice-5/gate-review-20261024/README.md)). Slice 7's claim, that an unavailable model holds with its cause, notices stop siblings before commit and a human can replace the agent of a bound run, is for Claude Code 2.1.287 with a delivered key or a login directory, a source-only engine profile demonstrated on recorded runs, stub tools and test doubles ([gate review](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/docs/evidence/m10/slice-7/gate-review-20261027/README.md)). A plan may select a catalog agent for every node of a run, which is approved under the V2 approval subject with its binding review. See [agent binding](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/spec/engine-v1/AGENT-BINDING.md#0-status-scope-and-non-goals) |
| Readiness 2.0.0 (`MODEL` capability kind, model set, configuration projection) | Implemented — SDK 0.4.0 in TypeScript, Rust and Python | The SDK part of M10, and its only one. Every SDK decodes 1.0.0 and 2.0.0 and encodes only 2.0.0, with three-language parity; the exported readiness types describe 2.0.0 and `v1` holds the 1.0.0 types. SDK readiness evaluation still takes 1.0.0 inputs only; the engine reads and evaluates both versions (see the engine readiness row below). Everything else in M10 is source-only. See [agent binding §9](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/spec/engine-v1/AGENT-BINDING.md#readiness-200) |
| Agent catalog and model register core | M10 slice 4 — built, source only | A source-only engine profile. The agent catalog is host configuration that pins each agent by capability digest; listing grants nothing. The model register is an append-only engine component of pins, offer status (listed, delisted) and prices, written only by a verified human holding `model-register` through a prepared command confirmed once (`control-cli register-action`, the web view's Model register section). A new coding run refuses any model set member that is not a registered, pinned, listed identifier; a delisting leaves bound runs dispatching. See [the record](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/docs/M10-MODEL-REGISTER.md) |
| Claude Code manifest and model assurance | M10 slice 4 — built, source only | A source-only engine profile for Claude Code 2.1.287 with a delivered key. The Claude Code host inspector reads the tool binary and the host settings files, never runs the tool, and reports the model set, the model-relevant configuration projection, `stream-json` usage reporting and the derived named gaps. It verifies each model confinement condition before dispatch; a run whose agent uses a model never dispatches without every one verified, a changed projection blocks dispatch, and a manifest whose named gaps differ from the derived ones is refused. A run whose agent has an empty model set may declare its cost not applicable, with its justification, and a run whose agent uses a model cannot. Confinement is observed configuration, not enforcement. The recipe is fixture-verified, and in the slice 4 live run the inspector verified it on the real installation and the tool served only the primary; how the tool applies each setting is from its documentation. Such an agent dispatches only through the Claude Code dispatch adapter, below. See [the record](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/docs/M10-MODEL-ASSURANCE.md) |
| Agent selection and binding review | M10 slice 4 — built, source only | A source-only engine profile. A plan selects a catalog agent for every node of a coding run in its `agent` field; without one the run binds the built-in local agent. The agent picker (`control-cli agent-picker`, `authoring-cli --interactive --agents`) lists every agent the catalog offers, and one that cannot be bound stays listed, not selectable, with the reasons of the first check that refuses it: a manifest refused or not the one the catalog pins, then a model set member the register refuses, then readiness BLOCKED for the draft plan. A run bound under readiness 2.0.0 records its node assignment and scope tree, dispatches only through the selected agent's installed adapter when it selects one (on the local worker when it selects none), and is approved under the V2 approval subject, which pins the node assignment, its readiness binding and the scope tree, not register prices or offer status; a run without a node assignment keeps its earlier subject. The binding review is one read model that the CLI preview (`control-cli authoring-preview`) prints for a draft, `control-cli binding-review` prints for a run, and the web view shows above its Approve button. One agent binds every node; per-node binding is not built. See [the record](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/docs/M10-AGENT-SELECTION.md) |
| Prices and allowance reservations | M10 slice 4 — built, source only | A source-only engine profile. A node whose agent uses a model declares an exposure allowance, its stop threshold and the run's cost bound, in ledger cost units; `authoring-cli --interactive --agents` asks for them once such an agent is picked. The run has a RUN scope and one NODE scope; every attempt reserves the whole allowance against both and pins the price table version in effect at the commit. A model set member without a price at that version, in the ledger cost unit, holds the node `PRICE_REQUIRED` before commit, with no attempt and no reservation; `control-cli hold-card` and the web view show its hold card, whose Add price exit opens the register's price sheet pre-filled with the missing keys, for a `model-register` holder to complete and confirm once. A price sheet that takes effect during an attempt applies only to later attempts, and a price in another unit is refused at write time. Settlement is the next row; the host meter enforces the stop threshold (its own row), and amounts are not shown in currency. See [the record](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/docs/M10-PRICES-RESERVATIONS.md) |
| Usage report and priced settlement | M10 slice 4 — built, source only | A source-only engine profile. A host installs a usage reporter with each harness; the Claude Code one turns an attempt's redacted `stream-json` output into its model usage report, never pricing it. Settlement prices the report line by line at the price table version the attempt's reservation pinned and rounds up once: a COMPLETE report settles at its priced cost, an INCOMPLETE report, no report or a line that version does not price at the full allowance, and an UNKNOWN attempt keeps its reservation whole, its settlement recorded `HELD_UNKNOWN` with no rule. The tool's own cost estimate is evidence only. Each priced attempt has at most one settled or `HELD_UNKNOWN` settlement record, and an overrun attempt at most one `HELD_OVERRUN` record, at the `RATE` basis for an agent with a delivered key or no credential and, since M10 slice 6, at the `LIST_EQUIVALENT` basis, by the same price table and rules, for an agent that keeps a login. `control-cli attempt-history` and the web view's attempt history show the basis, the priced and settled costs, the rule and the flags, with the priced lines on expand. A priced cost above the reservation settles nothing and holds the node (next row). Demonstrated on recorded Claude Code runs only, with no model request. See [the record](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/docs/M10-PRICED-SETTLEMENT.md) |
| Overrun and binding violation holds | M10 slice 4 — built, source only | A source-only engine profile. A priced cost above the reservation records the attempt's true cost and overrun at once, settles nothing and holds the node `EXPOSURE_EXCEEDED`; its hold card shows each scope's bound, use and whether it absorbs the true cost, and its Raise limits exit, for a `ledger-adjust` holder, raises the bounds through the engine ledger's human-only adjustment, after which the attempt settles at its true cost; a refusal leaves the node held. A model usage report entry outside the agent's model set holds the result `BINDING_VIOLATION` while the attempt keeps its outcome and its consumption settles; the run's approver may Discard it, giving the stage a fresh attempt, or Admit it with a written reason, after which it is marked "admitted with violation" on later screens. Each decision is recorded once. Both cards and their exits work in `control-cli hold-card` and `hold-exit` and in the web view. Replace is listed on the held result card but not built (the overrun card offers Raise limits and Cancel only). Since M10 slice 6 a login agent's reported credential source other than its login holds the result the same way (the reported credential source row). Demonstrated on recorded Claude Code runs only, with no model request. See [the record](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/docs/M10-OVERRUN-VIOLATION-HOLDS.md) |
| Host meter and stop threshold | M10 slice 5 — built, source only | A source-only engine profile for Claude Code 2.1.287 with a delivered key. A host installs a usage meter with each harness, beside its usage reporter: for Claude Code, `claudeCodeUsageMeter`, which reads the usage of each assistant message the tool streams. While an attempt of a node with a stop threshold runs, the local worker hands each line of its redacted output to the host meter, which prices the streamed usage at the price table version the reservation pinned, by the same code and rounding as settlement, and stops the attempt as its timeout does once the running cost reaches the stop threshold; a line that version does not price counts as reaching it. The stopped attempt is UNKNOWN and keeps its reservation whole until a human resolves it; nothing retries. The time limit and the meter stop the attempt's whole process tree through one tree stop, recorded in its evidence: a process group on POSIX and the job object of the opt-in Windows native helper, both proven, and `taskkill /T /F` on Windows without the helper, which can miss a descendant whose parent has already exited and is recorded as not proven. No engine host wires the native helper in, so a Windows host takes the `taskkill` path, and the helper is not tested on Windows arm64. On POSIX a process that calls `setsid` or `setpgid` leaves the attempt's group, and the stop does not reach it. A stopped tree is not proof that the tool's external effects did not happen. The attempt history in `control-cli attempt-history` and the web view shows where and why it stopped, and how its process tree was stopped. The Claude Code manifest declares the host meter, so it no longer names the gap "consumption not bounded during the attempt"; `--max-budget-usd` stays a backstop, and an agent without a host meter keeps the gap. A host built from a configuration module installs the meter itself, and the binding review says when a host has not. The final result is not metered, so an overrun is still held at settlement. Demonstrated on recorded Claude Code runs only, with no model request. See [the record](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/docs/M10-HOST-METER.md) |
| Model unavailability classification | M10 slice 7 — built, source only | A source-only engine profile. A host installs a model unavailability recogniser with each harness; after an attempt ends FAILED or UNKNOWN it reads the redacted output, and a cause it recognises (retired or not found, rate limited, overloaded, plan limit or spend limit) is recorded in the attempt's evidence. The attempt keeps its outcome and counts; a FAILED one settles as any other and an UNKNOWN one keeps its reservation whole. The node holds `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` with its cause, the model and any reported reset time, shown and never acted on; nothing retries by itself. A plan or spend limit records an account notice on the credential scope's account boundary, and a retired or unknown model of the bound model set an identifier notice; a notice also holds other nodes, as the next row says. The hold card, in `control-cli hold-card` and the web view, offers Reconcile, on a run bound to a workflow definition, Replace, which opens the reconcile-then-replace stepper on a hold after an attempt, and Cancel. For Claude Code 2.1.287 the recogniser reads the final result's API error status: only a refused unknown identifier is observed, and the plan limit is fixture-verified. A served tier below the requested one is evidence only. Demonstrated on recorded Claude Code runs only, with no model request. See [the record](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/docs/M10-MODEL-UNAVAILABILITY.md) |
| Claude Code dispatch adapter | M10 slice 4 — built, source only | A source-only engine profile for Claude Code 2.1.287 with a delivered key. `ClaudeCodeDispatchAdapter` runs each attempt of a bound agent with the projection its run pins: `--model` set to the primary, `--setting-sources user` with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` at the host config directory, `--no-session-persistence`, `stream-json` output, the fallback, subagent model and subprocess scrub variables, and `--max-budget-usd` from the stop threshold only when the ledger cost unit is a dollar unit, as a backstop, never a host meter; it passes the host meter on to the local worker, which stops the tool once its streamed usage reaches the stop threshold. A node command is `["claude", prompt]`. Before the claim it inspects its own host configuration and refuses when that would apply a projection other than the pinned one. The key reaches the tool only through `apiKeyHelper`, named by a per-attempt `--settings` file that carries nothing else, from a per-attempt directory only the host's OS user can read, deleted when the attempt ends, on UNKNOWN and at the release after a restart. Admission accepts `HELPER` delivery for this adapter alone; `FILE` is not built. Tested against a fake `claude` executable, and used by the slice 4 live run on Windows, where the tool reported the key source `apiKeyHelper` and served the primary; the tool's handling of its other flags is from its documentation, not observed |
| Agent setup and login directory | M10 slice 6 — built, source only | A source-only engine profile for Claude Code 2.1.287 on a subscription login. Agent setup needs the installation-scoped `agent-setup` permission, which the identity adapter's `authorize` receives with no work order. `control-cli agent-setup AGENT_ID create` and the web view's Agent setup section create the agent's login directory, its `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, readable only by the host's OS user and outside the workspace and artifact roots, write the reviewed configuration with the `forceLoginMethod` lock, and show the exact sign-in command, which the account holder runs personally; Praxis never runs the login flow and never reads, copies, stores or delivers the login. `agent-setup AGENT_ID check` runs `claude auth status --json` with only the directory pointer set and checks the login against the reviewed scope, keeping only the sign-in state, the login method and the account boundary; each step is prepared, reviewed and confirmed once, and the setup record names who and when. A run binds the agent only while its directory is set up and signed in under the reviewed scope, and the agent picker lists one that is not as not selectable, with the setup command. Before each attempt commits the probe runs again: not signed in holds `CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED` before commit with no attempt and no reservation, and another account or method blocks dispatch with `READINESS_BLOCKED`, which signing in again cannot clear. The login method field is documented by the tool; its account field is not, so the account boundary is recorded by the operator and checked only when the probe reports one. Probe outputs are fixture-verified, not observed. Reconnection is built: the `RECONNECT` exit of a login's `CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED` hold card, offered to an `agent-setup` holder in `control-cli hold-exit` and the web view beside the sign-in command, re-runs the probe and the scope check; signed in under the reviewed scope clears the hold and records who reconnected, when and the hold, starting no attempt, and another account or method is refused with `READINESS_BLOCKED`, durably, since it cannot be reconnected and the route is replacing the agent. Neither surface runs the sign-in. The exclusive hold is built: at most one attempt at a time holds the agent's login directory, from its commit until the ledger settles it or records it stopped, so one running or UNKNOWN keeps it until reconciliation, and a second attempt of the same agent waits, READY, with nothing probed, counted, reserved or held. Retirement is built: `agent-setup AGENT_ID retire` and the web view's Prepare retirement are refused, naming the attempt, while a running or UNKNOWN attempt holds the login directory, and otherwise mark it retired, so no attempt holds it again, run the tool's own `claude auth logout`, delete the directory and record whether each happened; the agent can then no longer be bound or dispatched. The reported credential source and a login's pricing are the next row. See [the record](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/docs/M10-AGENT-SETUP.md) |
| Reported credential source and a login's list-price equivalent | M10 slice 6 — built, source only | A source-only engine profile for Claude Code 2.1.287 on a subscription login. A host installs a credential source reader with each harness; after every attempt of a login agent, the Claude Code one reads `apiKeySource` from the tool's `system/init` event in its redacted output, and the runner records the source and its field in the attempt's evidence, keeping only a name the tool documents. A source other than the reviewed login, anything but `none` for Claude Code, holds the result `BINDING_VIOLATION` with a `CREDENTIAL_SOURCE` violation while the attempt keeps its outcome and its consumption settles: the hold card names the reviewed custody, the reported source and its field, the run's approver may Discard or Admit with a written reason, each recorded once, and Replace is listed but not built. An UNKNOWN attempt keeps its reservation whole and holds for reconciliation; a tool that reports nothing is not held, and a manifest that says so names `CREDENTIAL_SOURCE_NOT_REPORTED`. A login agent's consumption settles at `LIST_EQUIVALENT`: priced at the API list price through the same price table version, rules and rounding as `RATE`, with the basis recorded, and the host meter applies to it where its manifest declares one. `control-cli attempt-history` and the web view show the source on each attempt. The source is what the tool reports, and `none` also covers a bearer token or a third-party cloud provider. Tested against a fake `claude` executable, with no model request. See [the record](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/docs/M10-CREDENTIAL-SOURCE.md) |
| Availability notices and the notice list | M10 slice 7 — built, source only | A source-only engine profile. Before a credential is acquired, dispatch checks for a live availability notice on the agent's account boundary, on its primary model or withdrawing any member of its model set; one holds the node `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` before commit, with no attempt, no reservation and nothing to reconcile, so a sibling work order on the same account does not burn an attempt. An account notice expires at its reported reset time, and the next step then resolves the hold, naming no human, and rechecks every gate. A human resume is refused while a notice is live. A verified human holding `notice-clear` may clear an account notice or a retired-or-not-found identifier notice; a withdrawal or retirement-date notice is cleared only through the model register. `control-cli notices`, `control-cli notice-clear` and the web Notices section list and clear them. Demonstrated on recorded Claude Code runs only, with no model request. See [the record](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/docs/M10-AVAILABILITY-NOTICES.md) |
| Retirement dates and withdrawal | M10 slice 7 — built, source only | A source-only engine profile. A `model-register` holder withdraws an identifier (`control-cli register-action withdraw`, the web view's Model register section): an identifier notice then holds, before commit, every node whose model set contains it as any member, with Replace and Cancel as its exits, and only a reversal with a fresh pin basis clears it. A retirement date (`register-action retire`) is entered by hand from a provider notice, "not sooner than" as given; before it the binding review warns the approver, and from it new bindings refuse the identifier and a notice holds every node whose primary model it is. A date at or before now needs an explicit hold now. Binding refuses an operator-pinned member observed with weights other than its pin, and a re-pulled tag blocks dispatch with `READINESS_BLOCKED`. Replace, `RETIREMENT_CANCELLED` and the proposals inbox are not built. Dates are entered by hand; no provider was asked. See [the record](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/docs/M10-RETIREMENT-WITHDRAWAL.md) |
| Agent replacement on a run bound under readiness | M10 slice 7 — built, source only | A source-only engine profile, replacing the agent of every node of a coding run. `READINESS_PINNED` is no longer raised. A proposal may name its `successor`; the same agent id with a new capability digest is a valid successor, and the identical pair is refused with `SUCCESSOR_NOT_DISTINCT`. Before the human approves and again before commit, the runner evaluates the successor from a fresh host snapshot: READY under readiness 2.0.0 against the run's stated requirements and runner minimums, the binding-time credential checks, the agent catalog, the model register and the run's exposure; a failure refuses with `READINESS_BLOCKED`, `CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED` or the binding's own code and consumes nothing. Activation writes the successor's node assignment and readiness binding, one row per node assignment (readiness component version 3), and the approval names them; the superseded ones stay as history. Pricing, the model-set check and the register's bound usage read the current assignment. Nothing resets: a successor allowance that does not fit the remaining capacity activates with a warning, and dispatch holds `COST_LIMIT_EXHAUSTED` before commit, whose card offers Raise limits, the human ledger adjustment. After a failed attempt, activation is refused with `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED` until `RECONCILE_CODING`. Replace on a hold raised after an attempt opens the reconcile-then-replace stepper in `control-cli replace` and the web view. Each step is a prepared command with its own confirmation, and the stepper resumes at the step its records show. Before activation it shows the replacement review: the categorised manifest diff, the requirement and figure diffs, the remaining capacity, the account crossings and that nothing resets. Replacing from a hold raised before commit or from a held result, and naming a subset of nodes, are not built. See [agent replacement](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/spec/engine-v1/AGENT-REPLACEMENT.md) |
| Upgrade preflight for the attempt environment rule | M10 slice 2 — built, source only | A source-only engine profile. `control-cli upgrade-preflight` (text), the web view and `GET /engine/upgrade-preflight/v1` list each active coding run and every ambient host variable beyond the platform baseline it does not receive, flagging referenced and credential-like names; names only. See [agent binding §9](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/spec/engine-v1/AGENT-BINDING.md#attempt-environment-on-upgrade) |
| Attempt environment rule | M10 slice 3 — built, source only | A source-only engine profile and a breaking change. The local worker, which every engine-shipped adapter uses, builds every attempt's environment from nothing: the platform baseline (`TMPDIR` included, and on Windows also the variables Node's launcher supplies), the variables its adapter or the engine sets on purpose, and credentials delivered under HC-09. No other host variable reaches an attempt. The third layer carries a credential delivered under HC-09 (next row). See [agent binding §3](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/spec/engine-v1/AGENT-BINDING.md#attempt-environment-rule) |
| Credential admission and HC-09 delivery (test and command providers) | M10 slice 3 — built, source only | A source-only engine profile. For an API-key agent whose reviewed projection carries a delivered credential, the admission slot acquires it from the host HC-09 provider before the attempt commits. Unavailable, expired or revoked holds the node `CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED` before commit, with no attempt and no reservation, shown as a hold card (`aiws-hold-card/1`) in `control-cli hold-card` and the web view. The local worker redeems the handle at spawn into the attempt environment; the handle is released when the attempt ends, and a per-attempt credential is revoked, at once on UNKNOWN. A durable, nonsecret lease on the handle is written with the attempt's commit, so if the engine stops before the release, the restart releases the handle and revokes a per-attempt credential before any new dispatch, recording that the process stop is not proven. Providers are the in-memory test provider and the secret-manager command provider, which runs a host-configured argv command that prints the secret, with no shell and a timeout, at admission; a timeout or empty output holds `CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED` before commit, and nothing it prints is logged. At admission, a provider scope that differs from the reviewed scope refuses dispatch with `READINESS_BLOCKED`, which reconnecting cannot clear, and a credential that does not outlast the attempt's maximum duration plus a 60-second margin holds `CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED` before commit. Every secret the engine delivered is redacted from captured stdout, stderr and evidence before persistence, as `[REDACTED]`, including its URL, JSON and base64 forms; a secret shorter than 16 characters (UTF-16 code units) is refused at redemption, or by the command provider at acquisition, before commit; files the command writes are not redacted. An authentication failure that a recogniser the host installs for the reviewed harness recognises keeps the attempt's outcome, settled and counted (or UNKNOWN with its reservation), then holds the node `CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED` and holds every node bound to that credential before commit until a human rechecks it; the engine ships no recogniser for a named tool. Recheck is the hold card's prepared command, reviewed and confirmed once in the web view or `control-cli hold-exit`: it acquires the credential and checks it again without redeeming it. The hold card's Cancel exit is available, Reconcile on a run bound to a workflow definition, and Replace (via the stepper) on a hold after an attempt. See [agent binding §3](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/spec/engine-v1/AGENT-BINDING.md#delivered-credentials) |
| Engine readiness 2.0.0 and runs bound under readiness 1.0.0 | M10 slice 2 — built, source only | A source-only engine profile. Praxis decodes and evaluates readiness 1.0.0 and 2.0.0, evaluating each run under the version its binding names, and binds new coding runs under 2.0.0; a 1.0.0 binding for new work is refused with `READINESS_VERSION_RETIRED`. A run bound under 1.0.0 before the upgrade keeps its reviewed binding and 1.0.0 semantics until it ends. The operator view, its CLI JSON and the web view show each pinned run's readiness version. Agent replacement, the route from 1.0.0 onto 2.0.0, is built in slice 7: the successor binds under 2.0.0 and the 1.0.0 binding stays as history. See [agent binding §9](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/spec/engine-v1/AGENT-BINDING.md#runs-bound-under-readiness-100) |

## A useful current application boundary

Applications can use the libraries now to govern an adapter-driven workflow, persist its control history, retain uncertainty, inspect outcomes and emit telemetry. They still need a host that invokes the coordinator and supplies the trusted services above. The [tutorial](./tutorial.md) demonstrates this boundary without inventing scheduler or handoff APIs.

No npm, crates.io or PyPI publication is implied by the package names. Download the supplied packages or use the source workspace. SDK 0.4.0 and proposed standard edition 0.4 are different version numbers with different purposes.


## M2 source additions

All three SDKs implement immutable handoffs, per-consumer receipt claims, atomic admission, resumable RUN/BRANCH holds, pinned join inputs, artifact verification, deterministic reports, metric counts and a correlated durable notification outbox. See [handoffs](./handoffs.md) for equivalent examples and exact API boundaries. Work order = mission is an accepted identity. Full scheduling, worker lifecycle and dynamic graph changes remain Praxis work.

## M3 source additions

All three SDKs provide the opt-in `aiws-limits/1` ledger: hierarchical cost, active-time, elapsed-time and attempt accounting; protected handoff allowance; ancestor/dependency admission gates; durable reservations, stop/settlement evidence and human-only adjustment. Read [budgets](./budgets.md) for equivalent programs and required host ordering. No cross-database atomic commit, external cancellation service or automatic import of historical running work is claimed. M3 APIs ship in the SDK 0.4.0 packages and are absent from the older 0.3.0 downloads.

## M5 Praxis source boundary

The separate TypeScript `engine/` package now has executable SQLite, scheduler, dispatch, worker, validation and control primitives. [Persistence and recovery tests](./engine-persistence.md) documents the verified storage slice and its limits. A [composed local coding workflow](./engine-coding-workflow.md) now executes approval through acceptance, including bounded correction and interrupted recovery. M5 is complete for the local Node 24 + SQLite profile; production identity enrollment and the M6 and M8 qualification obligations are outside it. Engine source APIs are not exports of the three SDK packages.


The M5 [local control profile](./engine-control-api.md) now provides authenticated HTTPS, CLI and web decisions for the composed workflow. Production enrollment/provider integrations, the complete command catalog, paged history and release qualification remain open.

## Protocol interoperability

M9 is complete as the scoped protocol-interoperability feature track; M8 remains the independent qualification track. The common Praxis source contract represents version-pinned MCP, A2A and AG-UI bindings while keeping external observations non-authoritative. MCP synchronous/Tasks, A2A 1.0 client/server and AG-UI 1.0 event-projection profiles are verified against pinned official packages. AG-UI authenticated human-control ingress is verified in M9.7; M9.8 verifies a durable cross-protocol registry and privacy-preserving telemetry projection in engine source; M9.9 verifies the executable pinned cross-protocol campaign: all 4 advertised profiles, all 16 required scenarios and all 16 executable checks passed. M9.10 completes the cross-language correlation helpers, runnable examples, operator/recovery documentation, exact compatibility matrix and scalable SVG architecture maps. Read [Praxis protocol interoperability](./engine-protocol-interoperability.md) and the repository `docs/M9-BUILD-PLAN.md` before generating integration code.

## Governed model binding

M10 is a parallel feature track; its contract, [agent binding](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/spec/engine-v1/AGENT-BINDING.md), is specified. Its only SDK part, readiness 2.0.0, ships in SDK 0.4.0 in TypeScript, Rust and Python. In source, the engine reads both readiness versions, binds new coding runs under 2.0.0 and finishes runs bound under 1.0.0 under 1.0.0, its upgrade preflight is built, the attempt environment rule is in effect for every attempt its local worker runs, and credential admission and delivery work with the in-memory test provider and the secret-manager command provider, with the `CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED` hold card and Recheck; the agent catalog and the model register core are built, and a new binding refuses any model set member that is not a registered, pinned, listed identifier; and the Claude Code host inspector verifies model confinement for Claude Code 2.1.287 with a delivered key, which dispatches through the Claude Code dispatch adapter with its key delivered through `apiKeyHelper`, as the slice 4 live run did, and for a subscription login whose agent setup created its login directory and checked its sign-in, probed again before each attempt commits; and a plan may select a catalog agent for every node of a run, whose node assignment the V2 approval subject pins and whose binding review `control-cli` and the web view render; and every attempt of a model-using node reserves its exposure allowance at a pinned price table version, is stopped by the host meter when the running cost of its streamed usage reaches the node's stop threshold, and settles by rule, at the priced cost of a complete model usage report or at the full allowance, shown in the attempt history; a missing price holds the node `PRICE_REQUIRED` before commit, a priced overrun holds `EXPOSURE_EXCEEDED` until a human raises the bounds, and a usage report entry outside the model set holds the result `BINDING_VIOLATION`, each with its hold card and exits in `control-cli` and the web view; and a failed attempt the adapter recognises as model unavailability holds `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` after the attempt, with its hold card, and records its availability notice, which holds sibling nodes `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` before commit until it expires or is cleared, in the notice list. Withdrawal, retirement dates, corrections and register proposals, the OS credential store and other credential providers, login custody beyond agent setup and the status probe, `CREDENTIAL_SOURCE` violations and agent replacement on a readiness-pinned run are a source-only engine profile, not yet implemented ([§0](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/spec/engine-v1/AGENT-BINDING.md#0-status-scope-and-non-goals), [§9](https://github.com/seanrobertwright/AI-WS-SDK/blob/main/spec/engine-v1/AGENT-BINDING.md#9-compatibility-and-migration)). Do not generate code against that engine profile yet. Read the repository `docs/M10-BUILD-PLAN.md` for its slices and claims.

## Dynamic client controls

M7 slice 8 adds native TypeScript/Rust/Python contracts and verified HTTPS clients, protected-input CLI and reviewed web controls. All eleven dynamic decisions share the existing authoritative Praxis semantics. See [native dynamic controls](./engine-dynamic-controls.md). The SDK 0.4.0 packages include them; the earlier 0.3.0 packages do not. Since 0.4.0, the SDK source's copy of the dynamic control schema admits an agent replacement proposal's optional `successor` (M10 slice 7); the 0.4.0 archives do not.
